target_customer: Operations teams at companies with factories, warehouses and fleets
problem: Physical operations make thousands of planning, scheduling, allocation and routing decisions; OpEra builds custom optimization engines that re-plan when conditions change.
business_model: B2B software, custom optimization engines via pilots (pricing not stated)
product_category: AI decision engine / operations research for supply chain

founders.name: Hindy Rossignol
education: BSc Machine Learning, UCL and NUS

technical_complexity.rationale: Optimization models over messy WMS, ERP and Excel data, recomputed on change, is hard operations research; founders hold MIT OR degrees.

defensibility.rationale: Custom models per customer; no documented data or integration moat yet.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Too early; no sources on incumbent responses.

market_need_then: Self-reported results from pilots (38% lower delivery cost for a retailer, 54% fewer unfulfilled orders for a marketplace), unverified; founders say they met on a delivery routing project for a major retailer.

branding.domain_note: Uses operatechnologies.com; the shorter opera.com name is not used.

brand_strength.rationale: Brand is new (Fall 2026); 'OpEra' collides with Opera browser and other uses; no press evidence.

outcome_analysis: OpEra is a Fall 2026 YC company founded by two MIT Operations Research Center graduates, still in pilots, so no outcome exists yet. The only sources are the YC page and launch post plus a Dealroom profile. The main risk visible is that established optimization vendors exist; no dated evidence about them was gathered.
notes: Batch is current-year (Fall 2026); too early for outcomes. No funding found. No dated competitors found (Nextmv funding coverage from 2021 is not near the batch). Founder background claims come from the YC page only. 'Turned down Palantir, Mercor, Stack AI offers' is founders' claim.
